A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same multimodal fusion research, substantially revised from GMF to SCFAE. Their complete text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable, and retained architectural elements and benchmarks support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original GMF experiments on VGGSound, ActivityNet, and FakeAVCeleb, plus CIFAR and ImageNet dimensionality studies in Appendices C–D.

after.justification: v2 reports original SCFAE evaluations, component ablations, gradient analyses, and additional runtime, branch-masking, and seed experiments, including Appendix B.

M1.justification: The expansion, shared/specific split, cyclic exchange, and reconstruction pipeline is retained. However, v2 adds GeLU and pre/post SwiGLU processing to v1's linear mappings and replaces MSE reconstruction with a cosine-based objective (Section 4; Appendix A). The separate GMF-MAE integration described in v1 Appendix I is no longer included.

E1.justification: v2 adds CMU-MOSEI audio-visual-text sentiment evaluation across available-modality combinations. It removes VGGSound event classification and the CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, and ImageNet dimensionality experiments from v1's appendices. ActivityNet retrieval and FakeAVCeleb detection remain.

E2.justification: ActivityNet comparisons add MISA, DrFuse, AADML, DI-VTR, CMKT, Coupled Mamba, DLF, and AdaMMS, among others (Tables 3). FakeAVCeleb adds ART-AVDF, MACB-DF, CAFR, and other methods, while UAVM and Joint-AV disappear from its reported comparison (v1 Table 7; v2 Table 4). These changes extend beyond the CLIP/CMMP naming difference.

E3.justification: Reported GMF/SCFAE training changes from SGD with 20 epochs to AdamW with warmup/cosine scheduling and 10 epochs on the retained datasets; default expansion changes from 4 to 2. FakeAVCeleb documents R(2+1)D-34 instead of -18. ActivityNet drops the 4096–4096 configuration and mAP@20. v2 also introduces controlled encoder probing and batch-size-1 FP32 profiling.

E4.justification: v2 adds component and reconstruction-metric ablations, expansion/boundary/loss-weight sensitivity, modality-order tests, and branch masking (Tables 7–11 and 14). Figure 4 and Table 6 directly examine gradient behavior, feature organization, and encoder degradation. Conversely, v1's CIFAR/ImageNet dimensionality-validation analyses are removed.

E5.justification: v1 specifies seed 1; its ImageNet ranges describe validation-checkpoint minima and maxima. v2 Appendix B.3 reports four additional trials with different seeds and ± summaries for FakeAVCeleb AUC and ActivityNet mAP@100. This is a limited extension: the dispersion statistic is unspecified, and uncertainty is not reported throughout the comparison tables.

E6.justification: ActivityNet 128–128 mAP@100 is 0.308 for v1 GMF and 0.321 for v2 SCFAE under revised method/training settings, so this is not a controlled same-setting gain. FakeAVCeleb's reported MDS ACC/AUC changes from 83.86/86.71 to 82.80/86.50, beyond rounding. v2 adds MOSEI and extensive analysis results while removing VGGSound, dimensionality-study, and hybrid-model results.

T1.justification: v1's constrained entropy objective survives as v2 Equation 1. However, the optimal-dimension and mapping theorems, PNP-to-reconstruction derivation, performance-bound conjecture, and their supporting derivations are removed. v2 instead gives a brief self-consistent-field formulation and qualitative gradient arguments; the residual discussion remains without v1's mathematical derivation.

C1.justification: v1 claims a PNP/entropy theory with an exhaustive proof and an inexpensive general frontend whose combinations surpass prior methods. v2 centers its contribution on complementary task/reconstruction forces, gradient-conflict avoidance, and encoder robustness. PNP becomes explicitly intuitive motivation, and the hybrid-SOTA contribution is dropped.

C2.justification: v2 develops substantive explanations involving task-driven routing, preservation of non-dominant encoders, complementary branch roles, and reconstruction-weight tradeoffs. It explicitly bounds applicability to separate-encoder fusion pipelines. These replace much of v1's charged-particle and performance-upper-bound interpretation; the dimensionality-related computational limitation is retained and made more explicit.

D1.justification: v2 documents activation choices, SwiGLU widths, revised optimization schedules, matrix costs, and profiling conditions. Conversely, v1's explicit FakeAVCeleb split procedure, frame/audio preprocessing, training batch-size/input-shape tables, and executable-style pseudocode are omitted. v2 adds a code-provision statement but supplies no direct access link.

R1.justification: Related work shifts from native/extended/general multimodal task categories to coupled versus decoupled fusion and gradient-stability positioning. The comparison framework and bibliography substantially expand to recent retrieval, missing-modality, and deepfake approaches, including Coupled Mamba, MCULoRA, DLF, and AdaMMS, alongside additional gradient-learning literature.

P1.justification: The title, terminology, abstract, introduction, related work, method explanation, and experimental narrative are extensively rewritten around gradient coherence. Experiments are organized by fusion challenges, and the appendices are substantially reorganized. The retained gradient/residual discussion moves from v1 Appendix A to v2 Appendix C.

P2.justification: v2 adopts a two-column main text, redraws the architecture, adds a teaser and gradient/t-SNE panels, and removes the physical-cell, dimensionality-study, and GMF-MAE illustrations. Tables are extensively restructured, including moving the expanded FakeAVCeleb comparison into the main text. Entropy, gradient-flow, and residual diagrams have identifiable retained or revised counterparts.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens support for the mechanism through component/branch ablations, gradient and encoder probes, and seed checks, addressing v1's limited direct component validation. It also recasts the claimed exhaustive PNP proof, acknowledged incomplete in v1 Appendix B, as intuition. These gains outweigh lost preprocessing, split, and pseudocode detail, although those omissions and the unclear positive-cosine reconstruction-loss convention in Equations 5–6 remain material weaknesses.
